key: The Sun with his dear eye beholds that quarter of the heavens which priests Have placed within the sacred cell.
s: A hymn of rushing drops and seated priests closes here; Sāyaṇa, on 9.10.9, takes the beholder not as the sun but as Indra, and the ‘sacred cell’ as the heart, where he sees the Soma even after it is drunk.

evidence.gloss: Sūra: Indra of great valour, with the eye of his own shining self, beholds the dear place set by the Adhvaryus in the cave, that is, in the heart: the Soma, even when it has been drunk.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Rig Veda 9.10.9 at [732,9]), the last of the hymn’s nine verses, after the flowing drops (vv.1 to 4) and the seven seated priests (v.7): plain sense faithful. Sāyaṇa glosses sūraḥ as suvīrya indraḥ, guhā as hṛdaye, and adds pītaṃ somam api abhi paśyati; his gloss on v.8 (pibāmi) sets up the drunk Soma. Wilson’s note 2 reads him the same way and names Benfey’s solar rendering, so ‘not as the sun but as Indra’ states the gloss’s effect, not an added idea.
